sources.title: Tagged interview note preserving the rope timing puzzle

claims.text: The source preserves one-hour total burn time per rope and asks for a 15-minute timing method; length-proportional timing is not a valid premise.
The two-rope schedule yields a reliable t=30 marker and a t=30 to t=45 interval of exactly 15 minutes under the standard independent-flame burn-time model.

rope B both ends after marker
boundary_tests.expected: remaining quantity completes in 15 minutes and at t=45
proof never assumes length proportional to time

findings: The preserved source fixes the classic nonuniform-rope timing puzzle: each rope has total one-end burn time of one hour and asks for a 15-minute interval.
The candidate correctly avoids the invalid assumption that half the physical length burns in half the time.

The two-rope event schedule is exact under the standard independent-flame model: A both ends creates t=30; B one end has then consumed 30 one-end-time units; lighting B second end consumes the remaining 30 at two units per minute, so the interval t=30 to t=45 is 15 minutes.
The candidate explicitly distinguishes a 15-minute interval from an event exactly 15 minutes after initial ignition, preventing a common overclaim.
No project experience or source details are fabricated; the Java block is presented only as an executable arithmetic representation of the invariant.
